description: Calculate liquid volume in a partially-filled horizontal cylindrical tank from fill level.

seo.title: Horizontal Tank Liquid Volume Calculator
seo.description: Partially Filled Horizontal Tank Volume Calculator — Calculate liquid volume in a partially-filled horizontal cylindrical tank from fill level with instant results & multiple unit support.

formula.explanation: Liquid volume = Cross-sectional area × Length. Cross-section = r²·arccos((r−h)/r) − (r−h)·√(2rh−h²) (circular segment formula). ×1000 converts m³ to liters. Where r = radius, h = fill height.

inputs.label: Liquid Fill Height
inputs.hint: From tank bottom, not exceeding diameter

content.introduction: Calculate the liquid volume in a partially filled horizontal cylinder using the circular segment area formula. This is the standard method for dipstick-to-volume conversion for horizontal fuel tanks, water trucks, and bulk storage.

example.description: 3m diameter × 6m horizontal tank filled to 1m height holds ~12,395 liters (out of 42,412 total at 100%).

faq.a: This gives a theoretical result for a perfect cylindrical shell with flat ends. Real tanks with dished heads or internal baffles require a strapping table calibration.

At h = r (half full), the volume is exactly half the total volume. Due to the circular geometry, fill height is not linear with volume: at 30% height you have ~25% volume, at 50% height you have exactly 50% volume.
